content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after a recent spike.
- Overestimates prices during the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting a lag in adjusting to recent price trends.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and remain elevated longer than actual prices, which then correct downward — indicating failure to capture mean reversion after volatility.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward lower prices when the true outcome shows a clear upward trend, especially in the latter half of the forecast window.
- When the 30-day history includes a recent high, model tends to forecast a lower peak and then underreact to subsequent price increases — suggesting poor sensitivity to recent momentum.
- Model fails to capture the true price trajectory when the last 5–7 days of history show strong upward momentum — underestimates the continuation of that trend.
- Model overcorrects after a sharp drop, forecasting a recovery too quickly or too aggressively — leading to overshoots in the following days.
- Model tends to underestimate the true price at the end of the forecast horizon, especially when the last 3–5 days of history show a clear upward trend — suggesting failure to recognize momentum carryover.
